blocks.title: Rows Do Not Shrink
blocks.text: DataLoader cuts round trips, never rows fetched. Only cost limits bound how many rows a query may touch.

blocks.text: Log SQL per request and read p99 before tuning. An unmeasured fix usually moves the work somewhere else instead of removing it.

caption.text: Part 2 of GRAPHQL N+1. Your GraphQL query looks tiny and fires 51 database round trips — 408ms of pure network wait for rows the DB could return in 10ms. This handbook walks the whole defense: why per-field resolvers explode, how DataLoader batches a tick's worth of loads into one `IN` query, the order contract that silently returns the wrong user when you get it wrong, and the cost limits that stop a hostile query before it runs. Ten pages, from the first symptom in your logs to the production checklist.
